items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to facilities utilized
by the Albany parking authority, compensation of board members of the Albany
parking authority, and increasing the amount of bonds of the Albany parking
authority authorized to be outstanding
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4106

SPONSOR: BRESLIN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to facilities
utilized by the Albany parking authority, compensation of board members
of the Albany parking authority, and increasing the amount of bonds of
the Albany parking authority authorized to be outstanding

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Amends subdivision 6 of section 1493-b of the public authorities 2 law,
as added by chapter 874 of the laws of 1982.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Under its current enabling legislation, the Albany Parking Authority
(ABA) is limited in what projects or infrastructure it can work on or
fund unless those projects directly involve or adjoin a physical parking
infrastructure (garages, lots or meters).This limitation means that,
even though its customer base is dependent on infrastructure within a
few blocks of where they park (i.e. lighting, sidewalks, bike lanes, and
green space), the APA cannot (when financially able) help support, main-
tain, repair or expand this public infrastructure.

The APA revenues are dependent on the overall economic development that
occurs in the City of Albany. The APA, as a component unit of the City
of Albany, would like to be able to help facilitate economic development
when it is financially able to do so, as it relates to increasing the
customer demand at its facilities. The APA's bond cap limit was estab-
lished as $50,000,000 in 1982 so that the Authority could build and
repair garages. Since then, the cost of garage construction has
increased exponentially, and therefore the APA requests the $50,000,000
cap be expanded by $25,000,000 to $75,000,000. This does not increase
any debt obligation of the City or State.

When the APA was created, it's Board Members were not allowed to be
compensated in anyway. However, the APA board meets frequently and has
substantial fiduciary responsibilities. Like other Authorities and
Boards in the City of Albany, the APA Board be should be allowed to be
compensated up to $5,000 per year per member. Such funding is compar-
ative to the Albany Water Board and would come at the discretion of the
APA and from its independent budget.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019/2020: S8910- Referred to Rules FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:  None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
